question.text: This was the largest boat of the three in Columbus's fleet. It ran aground due to incompetent piloting and was dismantled to build the first Spanish settlement in the New World.
question.clue: This ship, the largest and slowest of the three that Christopher Columbus used in his first voyage to the Americas.

swap.leadin: This conflict saw the formation of volunteer International Brigades to fight fascists as well as the bombing of Guernica by the German Condor Legion.
swap.text: Name this 1936 to 1939 war in which Nationalist forces rebelled against the government of President Manuel Azana.
swap.clue: The paramilitary Blueshirts were largely responsible for executing the White Terror during this conflict.

question.leadin: In 1099, Valencian soldiers scared away Almoravid invaders by placing this leader's body on his horse Bavieca, making it appear he had returned from the dead.
question.text: Name this legendary Spanish warrior, a mercenary who fought on behalf of the Emir of Zaragoza against King Alfonso XI of Castile before claiming Valencia as his own.
question.answerHtml: El Cid [or Rodrigo Díaz de Vivar; prompt on Díaz alone; or El Campeador or the Champion, or Le Cid]
question.clue: This ruler of Valencia who fought both for and against the Taifa of Zargoza.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the Counter-Reformation.
swap.text: This institution of the Counter-Reformation, whose first chief was Tomas de Torquemada, was established by Isabella I of Castile to root out Moriscos, Jews, and non-Catholics.
swap.answerHtml: Spanish Inquisition [or Tribunal of the Holy Office of the Inquisition]
swap.clue: Tomas de Torquemada led this organization, which used a seal that quoted Psalm 73, and frequently used the auto-da-fe to publicly burn heretics.

question.leadin: After Jose Sanjurjo died in a plane crash, this man's connections with Hitler and Mussolini allowed him to become Generalisimo and Head of State.
question.text: Name this man, who served as dictator of Spain after winning the Spanish Civil War.
question.clue: This leader created an air bridge using Junker-52s to deploy his Army of Africa in a coup against Manuel Azana's Popular Front.

swap.text: This Nationalist political party of Francisco Franco was consolidated with the JONS party to consolidate Franco's influence. Jose Primo de Rivera once led this party.
swap.clue: Two leaders of this party were buried within the Santa Cruz Basilica at the Valley of the Fallen.

question.leadin: Prior to the defeat of this force, one monarch claimed that she had "the heart and stomach of a king."
question.text: Name this invading military force which was hindered by the "Protestant wind" and defeated at the Battle of Gravelines ["gravf-leen"].
question.answerHtml: The Spanish Armada (or Grande y Felicísima Armada; prompt on “Spanish navy” and equivalents)
question.clue: The plan was for this force to join with one under Alessandro Farnese, but before that could happen, it participated in its first engagement off Eddystone.

swap.leadin: The County of Barcelona and this kingdom were once ruled by a monarchy called its namesake "Crown."
swap.text: Name this kingdom whose monarchs included Joanna the Mad and Henry VIII's first wife Catherine.
swap.clue: A princess of this kingdom was the first woman named as an ambassador to another European nation, in this case England.

question.leadin: The Islamic state based out of this city was established when Abd ar-Rahman I organized the remnants of Kulthum's garrison, who had been living there for a decade.
question.text: Identify this seat of a caliphate whose illustrious Great Mosque was purchased from the Visigoths and reconverted to a church under Alfonso X.
question.clue: Mozarabs like Paul Alvar and Eulogius were hanged in this city during its namesake "Martyrs Movement."

swap.text: In 1812, the Freemason Agustin Arguelles helped draft a liberal but short-lived Spanish constitution named for this Spanish city.
swap.clue: In the 15th century, this city became the base of the Spanish Treasure Fleet.

question.leadin: This city is home to the world's oldest functioning lighthouse, the Tower of Hercules, and was referred to as The Groyne in some archaic English contexts.
question.text: Name this city in northwestern Spain, home to the Royal Galician Academy.

swap.text: Members of this ethnic group were particularly active in the whaling industry, setting up a fishing village at Red Bay in Labrador. Whalers from this ethnic group were killed in a 1615 massacre perpetrated by locals in Iceland.
swap.clue: This ethnic group's whaling activities led to the creation of a pidgin described by Jon Olafsson, and 32 shipwrecked members of this ethnic group were murdered in Iceland in the 1615 "Slaying of the Spaniards."

question.leadin: This communist activist, who was nicknamed after a flower, proclaimed that "they shall not pass" while Madrid was under siege.
question.text: Name this longtime leader of the Communist Party of Spain in exile. She was elected to the Spanish parliament in 1977 following the restoration of democracy.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the spread of Calvinism out of its birthplace in Switzerland.
swap.text: Jeanne d'Albret, a queen of this non-French kingdom, also publicly converted to Calvinism and declared it the state religion in 1560; her son would later claim that "Paris is well worth a mass" when converting to Catholicism.
swap.clue: Another ruler of this kingdom was offered the French crown by Etienne Marcel during the Jacquerie.

question.leadin: The first and second "families" of bestiaries, as defined by Cambridge scholar M.R. James, derive in part from this book.
question.text: Name this massively influential seventh-century encyclopedia that compiles numerous classical sources on such topics as the trivium and quadrivium, as well as on its namesake lists of terms.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about Napoleon's acquaintances.
swap.text: Napoleon made this eldest brother of his King of Naples and then King of Spain.
swap.clue: Joachim Murat succeeded this man when he abruptly left the throne of Naples.

question.text: An uprising known as the Zamacolada occurred after this Spanish prime minister tried to establish an independent port in Basque territory. This man became known as the "Prince of the Peace" after negotiating the Second Treaty of San Ildefonso in 1796.
question.answerHtml: Manuel de <u>Godoy</u> [or Manuel <u>Godoy</u> y Alvarez de Faria]
question.clue: He became his country's first commander to adopt the title of generalisimo while leading troops in the War of the Oranges.

swap.leadin: This man allegedly refused to dine without his poison-resisting unicorn horn nearby, and he built and was buried in the Monastery of St. Thomas at Avila.
swap.text: Identify this man who was able to sell the monarchy on a pet piece of legislation following the Holy Child of La Guardia incident.
swap.clue: The Alhambra Decree, which expelled the Jews from Spain, was advocated by this Dominican Grand Inquisitor under Ferdinand and Isabella.

question.text: One of Abd-ar-Rahman's accomplishments was to oust Ordono the Bad from the throne of Leon and reinstall a ruler of this name dubbed the "Fat." Another king with this name ruled Navarre during the early 1000's and occupied both Castile and Leon during his reign.
question.clue: This name also held by a "Great" king who conquered Leon from Bermudo III and split his Iberian kingdom between his sons Ramiro, Gonzalo, and Garcia after his 1035 death.

swap.leadin: This battle was fought near a hill called La Cabeza near the Guadiana River.
swap.text: Name this 1195 battle, a stunning loss for Alfonso VIII of Castile during the Reconquista. After getting whipped by Abu Yusuf Ya'qub al-Mansur, Alfonso would later avenge this disaster at the Battle of Las Navas de Tolosa in 1212.
